Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nimbus Cloud Technologies Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nimbus Cloud Technologies' results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Product Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; David Kim, Chief Sales Officer; Rachel Torres, Chief Security Officer; and Theo Grant, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nimbus Cloud Technologies delivered exceptional results for the Q2, demonstrating the strength of our cloud platform and the increasing demand for our AI-driven solutions across diverse industries.

During the quarter, we focused on eight key strategic priorities:
1. Expanding our global reach through strategic partnerships.
2. Driving innovation in edge computing and IoT solutions.
3. Enhancing our commitment to open source technologies.
4. Strengthening our data privacy and compliance programs.
5. Investing in our employees' professional development.
6. Improving our operational efficiency through automation.
7. Fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.
8. Accelerating the adoption of sustainable cloud practices.

Thank you, operator, and good afternoon, everyone. This is Alex Rivera, and I'm excited to highlight one of our biggest growth engines: the explosive growth and adoption of AI/ML workloads on our platform. Nimbus Cloud Technologies has established itself as a leader in the cloud computing space, fueling hyperscale AI infrastructure with our vast fleet exceeding 2 million NVIDIA H100 and H200 GPUs, complemented by our custom NCT-TPU v4 accelerators. Today, I'll cover the key metrics, emerging trends, regional breakdowns, technical advancements, and our roadmap to harness this transformation.

Starting with the top-line figures, in Q2 FY2024, AI/ML workloads—including training, fine-tuning, inference, and rising retrieval-augmented generation pipelines—skyrocketed 162% year-over-year, surpassing our overall compute revenue expansion of 28%. This category now comprises 32% of our total remaining performance obligations, up from 18% last year, and powers 41% of our net new annual recurring revenue bookings. For perspective, AI/ML run-rate revenue reached $4.2 billion this quarter, with inference alone surging 210% YoY to claim 62% of total AI compute hours—a shift from the training-dominated era of 2022-2023.

Adoption metrics paint a compelling picture. More than 68% of our top 500 enterprise clients, including Fortune 100 giants akin to major streaming platforms and leading search engines, are running live AI/ML workloads on Nimbus Cloud, compared to 42% a year ago. Self-service uptake through our Nimbus AI Studio—our managed counterpart to tools like AWS SageMaker or Google Vertex AI—has boomed, with 145,000 new ML models launched in Q2, marking a 195% YoY jump. That's processing over 1.2 billion inference tokens per second at peak, on par with top-tier models like GPT-4o.

Key trends show evolution from massive pre-training to efficient inference and agentic AI. Training holds at 38% of AI compute, while inference leads at 62%, driven by applications in recommendations and agents. Generative AI dominates at 81%, but multimodal vision-language models like our NCT-VLM-7B grew 240% YoY. Edge adoption of Mixture-of-Experts architectures rose 35% QoQ, offering 4x better price-performance on our GPUs versus dense transformers. NVIDIA's Blackwell ramp has eased supply issues, slashing H100 waitlists by 70% and hitting 98% fulfillment within SLAs.

By region, North America anchors 54% of AI/ML RPO at $7.8 billion, powered by Bay Area labs and quant trading via our Quantum Network Fabric. APAC surges at 188% YoY for 28% share ($4.1 billion), with sovereign LLMs in Japan and India via 500-petaFLOP telco clusters. EMEA takes 15% ($2.2 billion), up 132% despite regs, thanks to FedRAMP and EU zones. LatAm and MEA are early at 3% but doubling, with fintech RAG wins.

On the tech side, we're pioneering: Q2 GA'd NCT-Inferentia 2 ASIC for 50% lower token costs than A100s, now 25% of inference. Nimbus ModelServe v2 with Ray boosts Llama 3.1 throughput 3.2x; AutoScaler ML cuts TCO 28%. NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD at 15 sites, AMD MI300X fast onboarding, open-sourced NCT-Quantize for 4-bit precision adopted by 12,000 devs.

Our pillars: capacity (92% utilization, $1.84 revenue/watt), ecosystem (2,500 Marketplace models, 22% attachments), profitability (68% AI margins vs. 52% overall, 3-year GenAI contracts at 40% discounts). Q3 guide: 140-155% YoY growth, 75% enterprise adoption by FY25-end. Risks like supply/energy offset by hydro DCs and cooling.

AI/ML is the new cloud foundation, and Nimbus is leading. Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. We are very pleased with our financial results for the Q2. Revenue increased by 15% year-over-year to $25.4 billion, exceeding our guidance for the quarter. Our gross margin was 68%, driven by our efficient cost management and economies of scale. Our operating margin was 34%.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before diving deeper into segment performance, let me address a critical macroeconomic influence on our results: currency fluctuations impacting revenue. As a global cloud leader with over 55% of revenue from outside the Americas, we're exposed to FX volatility, especially with the strong USD due to the Fed's rate stance.

The numbers: Q2 revenue hit $25.4 billion, up 15% reported YoY, but 18% on constant currency—stronger underlying momentum. FX headwinds trimmed $420 million or 1.7 points off growth, the third straight quarter of drag totaling $1.2 billion since Q4 FY2023, from USD up 8% vs. key currencies.

Regionally: Americas 56% ($14.2B, minimal FX); EMEA 26% ($6.6B), euro down 4.2% QoQ for $180M hit (2.8% of revenue), though CC growth 16% from AI workloads like our NCT AI platform, akin to Azure's Europe efforts. APAC 18% ($4.6B), $150M drag from yen down 5.1%, Japan reported 12% vs. 17% CC, but gaining share in 5G edge; India/SE Asia up 25% CC via NCT Global Pay.

FX swings are common—AWS saw boosts in FY2022, now headwinds like Microsoft's 200bps Azure hit. Our 40% non-USD billing hedged by $18B local costs.

Mitigations: 70% hedging on 12-month exposures (EUR/JPY/GBP/AUD) saved $300M this quarter; 85% new contracts local currency (up from 65%); 15 new edge zones for LCY billing with NCT Outposts.

AI (28% compute rev, up 40% YoY) cushions via sticky consumption. Q3 headwind $200-300M, CC guide 17-19%. If USD persists, up hedging to 80%, more localization like AWS Local Zones.

FX obscured strength, but CC shows resilience in $600B+ TAM. Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology strategy and roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan. We are committed to leading the way in cloud technology innovation. We are making significant investments in research and development to create cutting-edge solutions for our customers.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings discussion—wait, aligning to Q2 context—as we execute our growth strategy in cloud computing, let me update on data center expansion and capital expenditures, foundational to meeting AI/ML and sovereign cloud demand.

Q2 capex: $2.8 billion, up 22% YoY, at upper end of FY guide $10.5-11.5B, driven by 45% RPO growth, AI at 38% of backlog (up from 25%). Capex/revenue 28%, peer-competitive. Property/equip 85% ($2.4B); deployed 150,000+ NVIDIA H100/H200 GPUs, utilization to 92% via NCT AI Fabric with Kubernetes/DGX.

Added 650MW net capacity, total 5.2GW across 38 regions/128 AZs, 30% sequential rise post-supply fixes.

Regions:
- North America (55%): Phase 1 400MW Virginia US-East-3, liquid cooling PUE 1.08, AI wins from banks.
- EMEA (25%): Frankfurt/200MW Milan for GDPR/EU Data Act, 100% RE matching, 52% RPO growth incl. French gov.
- APAC (15%): 150MW Jakarta Phase 1, Singapore +100MW Blackwell-ready, 60% rev growth.
- LatAm/other (5%): Mexico 100MW groundwork for LGPD.

Efficiency: fleet PUE 1.12 (from 1.15), 18% data transfer cuts via 400Gbps Ethernet, 82% renewables for ESG pricing.

Q3 capex $2.9-3.1B, FY high-end; FY25 $13-15B AI-focused. ROI: 18-24mo payback, 85%+ margins on $28B RPO.

Disciplined capex fuels growth in 25% CAGR market. Now, I'll pass it over to Mike Chen to discuss our product roadmap and recent launches.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Elena. We recently launched AetherAI Sovereign, a groundbreaking solution designed to revolutionize sovereign AI inference and fine-tuning.

Thank you, Dr. Vasquez, and good afternoon. Let's explore our new service launches and stellar market reception, fueling Q2 records. Nimbus Cloud launched three majors: NCT Sovereign AI, EdgeUltra, CarbonZero PaaS—adding $285M new ARR, 45% QoQ launch bookings jump, expanding TAM into sovereign AI/sustainable compute.

NCT Sovereign AI (late Q1 GA): managed sovereign platform on NCT hypervisor/Hugging Face/Ray, GDPR/HIPAA/FedRAMP native, zero-knowledge proofs. Graviton-X ARM 40% better perf than Graviton4, $0.75/M tokens.

Traction: 450 adopters in 90 days—EU bank 2.5PB fraud, US health 1,200 GPUs federated learning. NRR 128%, EMEA 55% (320% YoY vs. Azure), APAC 30% Nikkei incl. $150M telco. 8% sovereign AI share per IDC.

EdgeUltra (mid-Q2): 5G MEC w/Ericsson/Nokia, 150-node net sub-10ms AR/VR/autos. Kubernetes/Istio/eBPF, $0.12/vCPU-hr (35% under Outposts).

1,200 beta devs, 62% paid conv, $92M ARR—AV OEM 70% egress save, retail 5K stores. Churn 0.4%, NA 48%, APAC 180% YoY displacing Alibaba.

CarbonZero (late Q2): 100% RE PaaS, liquid-cooled PUE<1.08, ML CarbonOptimizer/K8s/carbon-aware. Blockchain credits.

320 sign-ups $93M ARR—energy firm 55% Scope2 cut, EU auto net-zero. NRR 135%, EMEA 65% CBAM wins.

RPO +22% $18.2B, 68% multi-year $4.2M ACV. Unified API multi-cloud. Q4 bookings $2.8-3.1B, FY25 28-32% growth.

Launches affirm "Cloud Everywhere." I'll now hand it over to Lisa Patel to provide an update on our marketing initiatives and brand strategy.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Mike. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and driving demand for our innovative solutions.

Thank you, Mike, and good afternoon. As we review Q2, let's focus on our energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives—a vital pillar. In hyperscale cloud, where DCs use 2-3% global power per IEA, sustainability drives efficiency, costs, differentiation. Customers demand ESG proof amid EU CSRD/Calif SB253.

FY2023 PUE 1.22 (14% better from 1.42), beating industry 1.55; saved 2.8B kWh (250K homes), Scope2 emissions down 28% to 4.2M tCO2e.

RE: 82% matching (from 65%), 12GW PPAs—3.5GW Orsted North Sea EMEA, 1.2GW Adani India APAC. 95% 2024, 100% 24/7 CFE 2028.

Tech: direct-to-chip liquid cooling 60% AI racks (40% cooling cut), Graviton4 25% energy/flop better, Optimize AI 92% util (vs 75% Gartner), 1.1TWh save.

WUE 0.18 L/kWh (22% better), zero-water Singapore/Tokyo.

Regions: NA Virginia/Oregon <1.10 PUE hydro; EMEA Frankfurt/Paris 85% RE REPowerEU; APAC 70% local chain 15% Scope3 cut; LATAM Sao Paulo 85% CFE batteries.

ROI: $2.4B capex 3.2x return ($1.8B saves +$750M ESG bookings). Clients like pharma genomics migrate for ISO14064; API w/Net Zero Cloud.

$5B next 3yrs fusion/quantum. 220bps EBITDA lift. Green cloud $200B opp by 2030.

Next, I'd like to introduce David Kim, who will discuss our sales performance and customer acquisition strategies.

David Kim:
Thank you, Lisa. Our sales team has been instrumental in driving our strong growth in the Q2. We are focused on expanding our customer base and strengthening our existing relationships.

Thank you, Lisa. As we eye H2 2024/FY25, macro factors shape sales planning, but our diversified AI resilience shines via $18.7B RPO up 28% YoY.

Interest rates 5.25-5.50%: 5-7% traditional bookings dip (ERP/VDI), Compute/Storage seq slow 3%; offset by 65% AI-infused $10M+ TCV. FY24 growth high 22-25% vs 27% no macro (2pt hit).

Inflation 2.6% PCE: power +15% YoY (22% COGS), EMEA PUE +0.05; countered liquid H100/TPUs 25% w/FLOP cut, nuclear SMRs 1.2GW 2026 for 68-70% margins.

Recession: US PMI<50/China49; Fortune1000 POC +20-30%, SMB -4%; AI 31% compute (from18%), Elastic ARR +42% 500bps buffer.

EMEA28% rev: euro -8% 1.5pt hit, CC24%; sovereign €2.1B pipeline, +300bps H2.

APAC15%: China thaw/yen-12%/India slow; Tokyo/Singapore 30%+ telco edge.

LATAM5%: Brazil Pix 55%, BRL -1pt; Sao Paulo edge.

Geopolitics: multi-cloud 40% top50, +18% cross-sell; 95% US/EU sourcing.

FY24 rev $32.5-33.5B (modest cut), EBITDA 32-34%; FY25 25-28%. AI/sovereign/diversification to $50B+ 2027.

Now, I'll pass it over to Rachel Torres to discuss our security initiatives and commitment to data protection.

Rachel Torres:
Thank you, David. Security is paramount to our mission. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and ensuring the integrity of our cloud platform.

Thank you, David. Turning to our core strength: security and compliance certifications this quarter. In cloud, trust wins; regulated sectors (fin/health/gov/infra) 45% of $2.8B Q4-like Q2 rev, up18% YoY. Gartner: breaches $4.45M avg 2023 +15%.

Q2: 17 new/renewed certs, total 125+ across 22 countries, +25% YoY >IDC 12%.

US: FedRAMP High P-ATO NCT Compute/Storage, DoD IL5 $150M, fed ARR $450M.

Health: HITRUST r2 zero majors, HIPAA/HITECH AI Inference, 22% bookings, 5PB PHI <1ms.

Fin: PCI DSS4.0 quantum token, SOC2/1 TypeII Deloitte, Sentinel SIEM 2.7M threats MTTR14min -28%.

Europe: ISO27001/17/18 GDPR Frankfurt/Paris/Dublin, EUCS 95%, DACH 30% share.

APAC: IRAP Australia, APEC CBPR Singapore, Tokyo My Number 3 banks 42% growth.

$250M FY24 sec R&D +27%: zero-trust eBPF, ML Guard 10T logs, AMD SEV-SNP. 62% new ARR regulated, churn1.2% half benchmark.

Ahead: CCCS Canada Q2, NIST800-53 High DoD. Compliance = wallet share, 73% CISOs barrier per ESG.

Finally, I'd like to introduce Theo Grant, who will share insights into our innovation strategy and future growth opportunities.

Theo Grant:
Thank you, Rachel. We are constantly exploring new technologies and business models to drive innovation and create value for our customers.

Good afternoon. As FY24 closes strong at 28% rev growth from AI/digital/edge, here's our FY25 capex outlook/investments, conviction in genAI/transformation/edge. RPO $145B +35% YoY, multi-year commitments.

FY25 capex $16.5-18.5B (22-25% rev, +15-25% from FY24 $14.8B); Q4 FY24 $4.2B +18% QoQ hyperscale/GPU.

Categories align pillars: AI ubiquity/global resilience/sustainable efficiency.

Hyperscale DCs/capacity 55-60% $9-11B: 15 new campuses +1.2GW.
- Americas 50%: 500MW Virginia/Oregon US-East-3/West-2, exabyte NimbusStore GenAI, 300MW Q4 energized.
- EMEA 25%: $1.8B Frankfurt/Paris/Saudi 200MW stc JV Vision2030.
- APAC 25%: $2.2B Mumbai/Singapore/Jakarta 100MW liquid 5G Telkomsel.

InfiniBand400Gbps/NVMe-oF <100us vs Azure NDv5.

Compute/network 25-30% $4.2-5.5B: 150K H200/Blackwell +50K Graviton4 (30% fleet 40% TCO), 20 AI superclusters Anthropic-like, 800Gbps Broadcom RoCEv2 5x LLM traffic.

R&D/sustain/efficiency 10-15% $1.6-2.8B: PUE1.15 (from1.22) $800M liquid retrofits, 100% RE Orsted/NextEra >Google. $1B quantum IonQ/confidential enclaves.

Demand-led: AI bookings +60% QoQ >AWS17%, util85-90% payback<18mo. Diversify TSMC/Samsung.

Americas55%, APAC30% high-growth, EMEA regs favor. Quarterly updates, upside AI>$200B Gartner. Balance $25B cash net debt/EBITDA1.2x for M&A.

Building AI backbone, 25-30% EPS FY25. Back to Alex.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term sustainable growth.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Wolfe Research. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Given the impressive AI/ML growth numbers, can you talk more about any capacity constraints you're seeing and how you're prioritizing demand allocation across customer segments?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. Great question. As we highlighted, our AI/ML surge to 162% YoY has been phenomenal, but we're proactively managing capacity through the expansions Elena detailed—adding 650MW this quarter and planning 1.2GW more in FY25. No major constraints today with 92% utilization and NVIDIA ramps easing backlogs. We prioritize hyperscalers and enterprises with multi-year RPO commitments, which are 68% locked in, ensuring high-margin sticky revenue. Self-serve via AI Studio gets overflow capacity dynamically. This keeps us ahead, fulfilling 98% SLAs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Green with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Laura Green:
Thank you. On FX headwinds and the capex ramp to $16.5-18.5B next year, how should we think about the impact on margins and free cash flow generation?

Jordan Lee:
Hi Laura, thanks. FX shaved 1.7 points this quarter but expect milder $200-300M Q3; our 70% hedging and LCY shift mitigate. Capex up reflects demand, but efficiency—PUE 1.12, 92% util—keeps gross at 68%, op 34%. FY25 capex 22-25% rev yields payback <18mo, AI 68% margins boost overall. FCF strong with $25B cash; post-capex positive trajectory accelerates as RPO converts. Confident in EPS 25-30% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with RBC Capital Markets. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks for taking my question. With rising regs like EU AI Act, how are your recent security certifications helping win deals in government and regulated verticals, and any pipeline visibility there?

Theo Grant:
Thanks, Raj. Our 17 new certs this quarter, including FedRAMP High, HITRUST, PCI 4.0, and EUCS, are direct enablers—regulated now 62% new ARR, fed pipeline $450M ARR. Innovation ties in: confidential computing with SEV-SNP and ML Guard on 10T events fortify sovereign AI launches. Pipeline robust, e.g., DoD expansions and DACH banks, positioning for 25%+ CAGR as compliance barriers favor us over commoditized players.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Wong with Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.

Chris Wong:
Hi, thanks. Sustainability is increasingly important to investors—can you update on PUE trends, renewable matching progress, and how that's influencing customer decisions?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Chris. PUE at fleet 1.12, targeting 1.15 FY25 via liquid cooling in 60% racks and Optimize AI at 92% util. Renewables 82% now, 95% '24/100% CFE '28 with 12GW PPAs like Orsted/Adani. Influences big: ESG RFPs won $750M, clients citing ISO14064 for migrations. Ties to data center adds—Virginia 1.08 PUE, EMEA 85% RE—driving NRR 135% in green services.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions and your continued interest in Nimbus Cloud Technologies.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
